list.item: Find the first and second derivatives of $$f$$ .
Find the relative extrema of $$f$$ .
Find the inflection points of $$f$$ .

solution.paragraph: Using the Product Rule, we obtain

$$\begin{array}{l} {{f^{\prime}(x)}{= x\frac{d}{\mathit{dx}}\left( e^{- x} \right) + e^{- x}\frac{d}{\mathit{dx}}(x)}} \\ {\phantom{f^{\prime}(x)}{= - xe^{- x} + e^{- x} = \left( {1 - x} \right)e^{- x}}} \end{array}$$
Using the Product Rule once again, we obtain

$$\begin{array}{l} {{f^{''}(x)}{= \left( {1 - x} \right)\frac{d}{\mathit{dx}}\left( e^{- x} \right) + e^{- x}\frac{d}{\mathit{dx}}\left( {1 - x} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{f^{''}(x)}{= \left( {1 - x} \right)\left( {- e^{- x}} \right) + e^{- x}\left( {- 1} \right)}} \\ {\phantom{f^{''}(x)}{= - e^{- x} + xe^{- x} - e^{- x} = \left( {x - 2} \right)e^{- x}}} \end{array}$$

Since $$e^{- x} \neq 0$$ , we see that $$1 - x = 0$$ , and this gives $$1$$ as the only critical number of $$f$$ . The sign diagram of $$f^{\prime}$$ shown in the accompanying figure tells us that the point $$({1,e^{- 1}})$$ is a relative maximum of $$f$$ .

Above the number line plus symbols appear from the left extreme to just before the tick mark labeled 1. The number 0 appears above the tick mark 1. From just after 1, minus symbols appear and extend to the right extreme.

solution.paragraph: Setting $$f^{''}(x) = 0$$ gives $$x - 2 = 0$$ , so $$x = 2$$ is a candidate for an inflection point of $$f$$ . The sign diagram of $$f^{''}$$ (see the accompanying figure) shows that $$({2,2e^{- 2}})$$ is an inflection point of $$f$$ .
